t.E524.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for sodium hydroxide as 'not limited'. In the EU it is a Group I additive; it was included in the call for data for re-evaluation published by EFSA in 2016.
t.E524.body: Its sodium, like sodium from food, is almost completely absorbed in the gut (about 98%); the amount in the body is regulated mainly by the kidneys, which excrete the excess in the urine.
t.E524.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E524.prod: It is produced chemically by electrolysis of a sodium chloride solution or by the reaction of calcium hydroxide with sodium carbonate.
t.E524.regx.1: Group I additive (sodium hydroxide); permitted at quantum satis.
t.E524.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E524.summary: Sodium hydroxide (caustic soda). Used to remove bitterness from olives, for the crust of simit and pretzels, and in cocoa processing.
t.E524.what: It is a strong base (caustic soda) used to regulate acidity and to neutralise.
